_this_is_the_separate_numbers_video: boerne-establishing.json carries a _no_statistics block saying the connectMLS figures, when they arrived, belonged in a SEPARATE video rather than being retrofitted into the place-and-feel script. This is that video.
_fact_verification: SOURCE: connectMLS, pulled by Heath 2026-10-03. Filters: Single Residential, City = Boerne, closed sales. San Antonio contrast row uses the same filters.

AVERAGES, NOT MEDIANS. connectMLS's built-in report outputs averages only; the custom-view option crashed twice. The word 'average' appears in the spoken script AND on every stat plate. Never say or write 'median' about these figures.
Sept 2026 Boerne: 50 closings, average sale price $625,022, average CDOM 107 days, SP:LP 96%.
Sept 2025 Boerne: 64 closings, average sale price $755,770.
YoY on average price: 625022/755770 - 1 = -0.173000 exactly. Verified by arithmetic, not by trusting the report's own percentage. -17.3% is exact to 4 decimal places, not rounded.
Dollar drop: 755770 - 625022 = 130,748. Verified by arithmetic. This is the figure the hook plate counts down to.
San Antonio Sept 2026, same filters: $337,087 average, -1.2% YoY, 96 days, 99% SP:LP.

UNVERIFIABLE BY ME: the San Antonio -1.2% YoY. I have SA's current average but not SA's prior-year average, so I could not re-derive it the way I re-derived Boerne's -17.3%. It comes from the same connectMLS report as every other figure here and is stated as 'about one percent' in the voiceover rather than to a decimal. Flagged to Heath.

DELIBERATELY OMITTED: the 272 active listings and the ~5.4 months of inventory. 272/50 = 5.44, but that months-figure is OUR OWN calculation (actives divided by one month's closings), not a connectMLS output. feedback_triple-check-public-facing-facts.md: if a number cannot be stated cleanly, leave it out. Cutting it also buys runtime.
DELIBERATELY OMITTED: CDOM 107 vs 96 and SP:LP 96% vs 99%. Real and verified, but price IS the story and four more figures would dilute it past the 34s ceiling.
SAMPLE-SIZE HONESTY IS IN THE SCRIPT, not just in this file. The CAVEAT beat says one month and fifty sales out loud. A single month at n=50 is not a trend and the video must not imply it is.
SCOPE: all single-family closings in the city of Boerne. NOT isolated to resale, and the script does not claim it is.
_fiduciary_note: Heath is a listing agent with an active Boerne-area listing. listing-copy-never-signal-weakness.md bans conceding weakness in LISTING copy because he represents the seller. This is a market report, not listing copy for a property he represents, so the rule does not literally reach it -- but publishing a 17.3% decline in his own farm area is still a real consideration and is flagged to Heath in the handoff rather than decided here. Nothing in this script mentions any specific property, his own listings, or invites an offer.
_music_why: Same track and same measured gain as boerne-establishing.json -- highest drive of the 12 tracks (0.161), 132s so no loop seam under a ~32s cut, and -11 is the value already measured to put nominal separation at 19 dB for this denser bed. Licence-clean (Pixabay Content License). Reusing it also keeps the Boerne drone pieces sonically a set.
_cta_why: The measured problem is zero shares and near-zero comments across every published video. So the CTA is a forwarding instruction plus a question, not a follow ask. 'Send this to someone who owns in Boerne' gives the viewer a specific person to think of; the spoken line then asks what their own numbers show, which is answerable by any agent in the comments.
caption_rewrite: a hundred thirty thousand seven hundred forty eight dollars
_stat_timing: Timed to the WORD, not to the clock -- docs/VIDEO-PRODUCTION-RECIPE.md §7 records an annotation that fired at 4s for a clause not named until 19s and so pointed at the wrong moment. Measured against this build's own caption timeline at speed 1.12: the drop is spoken 2.14-4.21 (plate 1 runs 2.8-5.4, starting after the hook card clears at 2.70 so two large-type layers never stack); '17.3%' lands 12.32-14.99 (plate 2 runs 12.4-14.9); 'San Antonio, same filters, down about 1%' runs 15.07-18.73 (plate 3 runs 15.1-18.6). Re-derive these if the script changes.
_sa_precision: Plate 3's sub says 'DOWN ABOUT 1%', not '-1.2%'. The -1.2% is the one figure in this spec I could not re-derive by arithmetic (no SA prior-year average on hand), so the precise number is kept off screen and out of the voiceover and the hedge is used in both.
_stat_why: Three plates, not six. The first COUNTS DOWN from last September's average to this one, so the viewer watches the money come off before Heath says a word about it -- that fall is the whole point of the piece and it is the one thing a static card cannot do. The second holds the percentage. The third is the contrast that makes it forwardable: the same filters in San Antonio barely moved. Plates sit at MarginV 430 (upper-middle), clear of the caption box at MarginV 1005 and of the hook at 170.

beats.text: Boerne's average sale price dropped over a hundred thirty thousand dollars in one year.
Fifty closings last month averaged six hundred twenty five thousand. A year ago, seven hundred fifty five thousand.
San Antonio, same filters, down about one percent.
This is a Boerne correction, not a Texas one.
One month, fifty sales, and these are averages, not medians.
But if you own in Boerne, that changes your spring plan.
Send this to someone who owns here. What are your numbers showing?

_runtime_cut: First build of this script ran 45.40s against a 21-34s ceiling, so every beat was tightened. NOTHING was dropped -- all eight beats survive, including the closing benefit clause and the caveat, which are the two lines founder-video-production-standard.md §5 says must never be the thing you cut. The runtime came out of redundancy ('So this is a Boerne correction. It is not a Texas one.' -> 'This is a Boerne correction, not a Texas one.'), not out of content. The hook now says 'over a hundred thirty thousand' where it used to say the exact 130,748; the exact figure is still on the hook card and is still true -- 130,748 is over 130,000.
_closing_clause: The final spoken line is the CTA beat in full. Dropped lines: NONE.
_shot_rhythm: Evergreen clips only. The library is December 2024 footage and roughly a third of it carries Christmas decoration (tree, nutcrackers, SEASONS GREETINGS lettering, the Hickok bronze in a Santa hat) -- holiday decor under an October market report dates the video instantly and reads as stock. Every clip below is an aerial or an undecorated exterior. Cuts 1.7-2.1s, hero open and hero close.
_water_clip_cut: First build put city-lake and creek-mirror clips in the rotation and the 13.0s verification frame came back as murky green pond water with floating debris -- the exact failure trec-5e-time-of-essence.json already logged ("frames read as murky pond water"). LIBRARY.md also warns the 9:16 crops of the creek clips keep only water and sky. Replaced with clips that carry recognisable PLACE: the BOERNE mural reveal (the word is legible), the plaza approach to the bandstand, and a second rooftops angle. The remaining water shots are the cypress-lined creek and the bridge approach, which read as landscape rather than pond.
_broll_gate: Every clip above is marked 'clear' in Media/b-roll/boerne/LIBRARY.md. The 6 flagged clips (main-street-shops x2 faces, main-street-shops-b x2 plates, neighborhood-aerial x2 private property) are not referenced and resolve_clip() would refuse them anyway. The neighbourhood aerial is the tempting one for a housing-market video and it is exactly the one that is gated -- individual private residences, identifiable and locatable.
_cover_t_why: 4.0s lands after the hook card clears (2.7s) and inside the first stat plate's settled figure, so the poster frame carries the $625,022 plate over the Main Street aerial rather than a bare landscape.
